gloss: one step; a small amount of progress

definitions.explanation: A single step or pace when walking.
Figuratively, a small advancement or movement toward a goal.

examples.japanese: {一歩|いっぽ}{前|まえ}に{出|で}る。
{一歩|いっぽ}も{動|うご}けなかった。
examples.english: I couldn't move a single step.

examples.japanese: {彼|かれ}は{一歩|いっぽ}{引|ひ}いて{見|み}ていた。
{夢|ゆめ}に{一歩|いっぽ}{近|ちか}づいた。
examples.english: I got one step closer to my dream.

examples.japanese: {改革|かいかく}の{第|だい}{一歩|いっぽ}を{踏|ふ}み{出|だ}した。
examples.english: We took the first step toward reform.

examples.japanese: {成功|せいこう}への{一歩|いっぽ}として{経験|けいけん}を{積|つ}む。
examples.english: I gain experience as a step toward success.

notes:
{一歩|いっぽ} means both a literal single step and figurative progress.

COMMON PATTERNS (Sense 1):
- {一歩|いっぽ}{前|まえ}へ: one step forward
- {一歩|いっぽ}{後|あと}へ: one step back
- {一歩|いっぽ}も{引|ひ}かない: not give an inch
- {一歩|いっぽ}も{動|うご}けない: cannot move at all

FIGURATIVE EXPRESSIONS (Sense 2):
- {第|だい}{一歩|いっぽ}: first step
- {一歩|いっぽ}{一歩|いっぽ}: step by step
- {一歩|いっぽ}{先|さき}を{行|い}く: to be one step ahead
- {一歩|いっぽ}{手前|てまえ}: one step short of, on the verge of

RELATED WORDS:
- {二歩|にほ}: two steps (also illegal move in shogi)
- {何歩|なんぽ}: how many steps
